Within this context, it is impossible for them to divulge the sources of this research and the goals pursued, because that could immediately point any possible rivals down the most beneficial avenues. Cover-ups and disinformation (both active as well as passive) would still remain, under this hypothesis, an absolute necessity.

    Thus it would appear natural that in the minds of U.S. military leaders, secrecy must be maintained as long as possible.

    Only increasing pressure from public opinion, possibly supported by the results of independent researchers, by more or less calculated disclosures, or by a sudden rise in UFO manifestations, might perhaps induce U.S. leaders and persons of authority to change their stance.

    It does not seem that we have arrived at that point yet.

BACK IN JANUARY, Agence France Presse reported that a Siberian airport was shut for 1½ hours while a luminescent unidentified flying object hovered above its runway. Although it's hard to imagine such an event taking place in the industrialized United States, a compelling October 2000 study by a retired aerospace scientist from NASA-Ames Research Center shows that similar incidents have occurred in America's skies over the last 50 years. "Aviation Safety in America — A Previously Neglected Factor" presents more than 100 pilot and crew reports of encounters with unidentified aerial phenomena (UAP) that appear to have compromised aviation safety.

Author Richard F. Haines, formerly NASA's chief of the Space Human Factors Office and a Raytheon contract scientist, is chief scientist for the National Aviation Reporting Center on Anomalous Phenomena (NAR-CAP), a research organization founded last year. In stunning detail, pilots and crew describe a range of geometric forms and lights inconsistent with known aircraft or natural phenomena. Bizarre objects paced aircraft at relatively near distances, sometimes disabling cockpit instruments, interrupting ground communications, or distracting the crew.

The data include 56 near-misses. Impulsive responses by pilots to an approaching high-speed object can be hazardous; in a few cases, such violent evasive reactions injured passengers and flight attendants. However, Haines states that there is no threat of a collision caused directly by UAP "because of the re-ported high degree of maneuverability shown by the UAP." While flying over Lake Michigan in 1981, TWA Capt. Phil Schultz saw a "large, round, silver metal object" with dark portholes equally spaced around the circumference that "descended into the atmosphere from above," according to his hand-written report. Schultz and his first officer braced themselves for a mid-air collision; the object suddenly made a high-speed turn and departed.

Veteran Japan Airlines 747 Capt. Kenju Terauchi reported a spectacular prolonged encounter over Alaska in 1986. "Most unexpectedly, two space ships stopped in front of our face, shooting off lights," he said. "The inside cockpit shined brightly and I felt warm in the face." Despite the Federal Aviation Administration's determination that he and his crew were stable, competent and professional, he was grounded for speaking out.

In 1997, a Swissair Boeing 747 over Long Island just missed a glowing, white, cylindrical object speeding toward the plane. According to an FAA Civil Aviation Security Office memorandum, pilot Philip Bobet said that "if the object was any lower, it may have hit the right wing."

Ground-systems operators have also been affected by UAP. "The element of surprise means a decrease in safety because it diverts the attention of air-traffic controllers that should be focused on landing planes. That is a danger," says Jim McClenahan, a recently retired FAA air-traffic-control specialist and NARCAP technical adviser. "Aviation Safety in America" does not attempt to explain the origin of these mysterious objects. But Haines writes that hundreds of reports, some dating back to the 1940s, "suggest that they [UAPs] are associated with a very high degree of intelligence, deliberate flight control, and advanced energy management."

In the 1950s, pilots and crews reported seeing flying discs, cigar-shaped craft with portholes, and gyrating lights, all with extraordinary technical capabilities. Documents show the unexplained objects were considered a national security concern. By order of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, commercial pilots were required to report sightings and the un-

authorized release of a UFO report could cost them 10 years in prison or a $10,000 fine.

To keep this information from the public, officials ridiculed and debunked legitimate sightings, angering some pilots. According to the Newark Star Ledger in 1958, more than 50 commercial pilots who had reported sightings, each with at least 15 years of major airline experience, blasted the censorship policy and denials as "bordering on the absolutely ridiculous."

These pilots said they were interrogated by the Air Force, sometimes all night long, and then "treated like incompetents and told to keep quiet," according to one pilot. "The Air Force tells you that the thing that paced your plane for 15 minutes was a mirage or a bolt of lightening," he told the Star-Ledger. "Nuts to that. Who needs it?" As a result, many pilots "forget" to report their sightings at all, one pilot said.

According to a 1952 Air Force Status Report on UFOs for the Air Technical Intelligence Center, pilots were so humiliated that one told investigators, "If a space ship flew wing-tip to wing-tip formation with me, I would not report it." The vast majority of sightings by American pilots are still not reported. The media perpetuate the censorship and ridicule, handicapping the collection of valuable data.

In contrast, other countries are openly investigating the impact of UAP on aviation safety. A 1999 French study by retired generals from the French Institute of Higher Studies for National Defense and a government agency with the National Center for Space Studies examined hundreds of well-documented pilot reports from around the world. The study could not explain a 1994 Air France viewing of a UAP that instantaneously disappeared as confirmed by radar and a 1995 Aerolineas Argentinas Boeing 727 encounter with a luminous object that extinguished airport lights as the plane attempted to land.

"Aeronautic personnel must be sensitized and prepared to deal with the situation," the report states. They must first "accept the possibility of the presence of extraterrestrial craft in our sky." Then, "it is necessary to overcome the fear of ridicule."

The National Aviation Reporting Center for Anomalous Phenomena (NARCAP) is a
national organization, established in November of 2000, and is dedicated to the
advancement of aviation safety issues as they apply to Unidentified Aerial Phenomena
(UAP).

NARCAP investigates aviation related reports of aerial encounters with lights or objects
that seem inconsistent with known categories of aircraft and common natural phenomena.
These lights or objects are reported to appear in a variety of colors and shapes. Pilots, air
traffic controllers and radar operators report that these lights or objects closely approach
aircraft. Encounters with these lights or objects, UAP, have a demonstrated a variety of
safety related effects on pilots, crew, cockpit discipline and on-board instrumentation.

NARCAP Chief Scientist Dr. Richard F. Haines has compiled a catalogue of over 3400
aviation related UAP cases. He has conducted a comprehensive review of UAP reports by
U.S. air traffic controllers and pilots from the past 50 years. A result of this effort is
Richard's paper" Aviation Safety in America- A Previously Neglected Factor". It
contains analyses of over one hundred reports of UAP involved in near misses, close
pacing, disrupted avionics, and collisions. These events were reported by US military
aviators, civil aviation professionals, private pilots, and by foreign aircrews operating in
US airspace.

NARCAP has no basis for conjecture regarding the true nature or source of these lights
and objects. It is the NARCAP position that certain unidentified aerial phenomena have
an effect on aviation safety that can be quantified. It is the intention of this organization
to develop a body of data that will stand up to scientific scrutiny and serve as a basis for
understanding this phenomenon.

It is our hope that aviation professionals will recognize the importance of this work and
contact NARCAP with their reports of encounters with UAP. Often, though not always,
reporters are concerned about their confidentiality. We are not associated with the FAA
or other government agencies, or the airlines. With regards to employers, the FAA, and
the media, we have a process in place to ensure that confidentiality is protected.

translationJa.fullTextJa: P.A.O.リリース用のGemini 7/6飛行解説テープ。管制センターのマスターテープから複製され、粒子だけでなく未確認物体とブースターへの言及を含む会話として再生される。HoustonがGemini 7に通信状態を確認し、Bormanは「10時方向高所にbogeyがある」と報告する。Houstonは、それがブースターなのか自然現象なのかを確認しようとするが、Bormanは「ここにデブリがあり、これは実際の視認だ」と述べる。距離や大きさを尋ねられると、Bormanはブースターも視認しており、左側を数百個の小さな粒子が3、4マイルほど外側で通過しているように見えると説明する。粒子は車両の進路に対して90度の経路のように見え、やがて通過して極軌道に入っていくように見えたとされる。Lovellは自分の側にブースターがあり、黒い背景に太陽光を受けた明るい物体として見え、その周囲に非常に多くの粒子があると述べる。Houstonは方向を尋ね、Lovellは2時方向前方でゆっくり回転していると答える。最後にGemini Controlは、この会話中の第三の未確認物体への言及は「bogey」であり、飛行4時間24分時点の交信だったと説明する。
translationJa.summaryJa: Gemini 7の交信記録。乗員が10時方向高所の「bogey」と、多数の小さな粒子、ブースターを視認したと報告している。
translationJa.summaryEn: Gemini 7 air-to-ground transcript in which the crew reports a bogey high at ten o'clock, many small particles, and the booster in sight.

translationJa.summaryJa: 1944年12月以降、415th Night Fighter Squadronなどの搭乗員が夜間に説明不能な光・物体を複数報告した。報告には、点滅や色の変化を伴う灯火が飛行機に追随する事例や、アルミ色で長さ約12フィート・直径約1フィートの円筒状物体が垂直に浮き下端に小さなフィンが突出しているように見え、攻撃されて一部しぼみ赤い炎を上げたが煙は出ず分解はしなかった、という記述が含まれる。これらの目撃は出撃報告に記録され、写真撮影が試みられたが成功しなかった。関係部隊は事案をSHAEFおよび英国Air Ministryに照会し、技術諜報担当者の現地訪問と更なる調査を要請した。Air Ministryは一部をMe.262戦闘機、残りを対空ロケット（flak rockets）が最もあり得る説明と述べつつ、証拠は断片的で多様なため決定的な結論は出せないと回答している。
translationJa.summaryEn: From December 1944 onward, aircrews—notably the 415th Night Fighter Squadron—reported multiple unexplained night phenomena. Reports describe blinking, color-changing lights that accompanied aircraft and a separate account of an aluminium-colored cylindrical object about 12 ft long and 1 ft diameter, appearing vertically suspended with small fins, partially deflated after attack and producing a red flame without smoke; it did not disintegrate. Sightings were recorded in sortie reports and photographic attempts were unsuccessful. The incidents were forwarded to SHAEF and the Air Ministry, and a visit by a technical intelligence officer and further investigation were requested. The Air Ministry noted some reports might involve Me 262 aircraft and suggested flak rockets as the most likely explanation for others, but judged the evidence sketchy and gave no definitive conclusion.

From OI OB

     Following report on unidentified aircraft sighting comes from 307th Bomb
Group which participated in operation daggar.  Unidentified aircraft was
sighted by three crews of the group at 1402Z 5 Sep 48 off west coast of Holland,
5155N/0355E.  Altitude of all aircraft was 30,000 feet.  When first sighted
the unidentified A/C was cruising at a normal jet speed, heading 120 degrees.
Soon after first seen, A/C began leaving smoke trails and condensation trails
accompanied by sudden acceleration and then climb.  Generall agreed by
observers that it was a single jet propelled A/C employing probably rocket
assists with tremendous reserve power, more than normal curising speed for
jets of the 1947 variety.  Never within identification range; its course
did not indicate its purpose.

        USAFE 14          TT 1524     TOP SECRET        4 Nov 1948


From OI OB

        For some time we have been concerned by the recurring reports on flying
saucers.  They periodically continue to cop up; during the last week, one was
observed hovering over Neubiberg Air Base for about thirty minutes.  They
have been reported by so many sources and from such a variety of places that
we are convinced that they cannot be disregarded and must be explained on some
basis which is perhaps slightly beyond the scope of our present intelligence
thinking.

        When officers of this Directorate recently visited the Swedish Air
Intelligence Service.  This question was put to the Swedes.  Their answer
was that some reliable and fully technically qualified people have reached
the conclusion that "these phenomena are obviously the result of a high
technical skill which cannot be credited to any presently known culture on
earth."  They are therefore assuming that these objects originate from some
previously unknown or unidentified technology, possibly outside the earth.

        One of these objects was observed by a Swedish technical expert near
his home on the edge of a lake.  The object crashed or landed in the lake
and he carefully noted its azimuth from his point of observation.  Swedish
intelligence was sufficiently confident in his observation that a naval
salvage team was sent to the lake.  Operations were underway during the
visit of USAFE officers.  Divers had discovered a previously uncharted
crater on the floor of the lake.  No further information is available, but
we have been promised knowledge of the results.  In their opinion, the
observation was reliable, and they believe that the depression on the floor
of the lake, which did not appear on current hydrographic charts, was in
fact caused by a flying saucer.

        Although accepting this theory of the origin of these objects poses a
whole new group of questions and puts much of our thinking in a changed
light, we are inclined not to discredit entirely this somewhat spectacular
theory, meantime keeping an open mind on the subject.  What are your
reactions?

TOP SECRET

(END OF USAFE ITEM 14)

He also knows of a Soviet-built radar set located near Kholomia Airfield
(5 KM W of Airfield, near the town of Kholomia). This type set is
called "Redut". He believes personnel of this set to be army, assigned
to PVO, but is not certain. His regiment conducted flying cooperation
exercises with the set, presumably to train the set operators, since
the set was first located at Kholomia in Spring 1947. His aircraft, in
October 1948, lost the set on such an exercise at a distance of 150 kilometers
and altitude of 1200 meters. Following instructions, he then climbed to
3000 meters, when the set again picked him up. he states he believes this
type set is standard throughout the PVO, and that he believes its maximum
range to be 150 kilometers, because no training flights of greater distances
were ever undertaken. Further details will be sought.

     All TU-2 of 63 Regt are fitted with IFF type S. CH. (C-4), located
in the tail of the aircraft and operated by a switch in the radio operator's
compartment. Further, experiments with airborne radar (a tail warning
device) werecarried out in 1947 and TU-2 of his regiment. This equipment
involved the installation of a small external array. Sets were removed after
a few days of testing, but results were understood to have been satisfactory.

     On the subject of Kholomia Airfield, this field is currently apparently
simply a level pasture, 600 meters N/S by 1400 meters E/W, but a paved runway
is being constructed outside the north boundary of the airfield. No details
are known to subject, as work has just commenced. The airfield currently has
no installations; aircraft are parked in the open, and fuel is brought
directly to the aircraft from the town of Kholomia (7 kilometers to the N) by
tank trucks.

     Another interesting fact is the arrival of the TU-2 with only a crew
of three, and without the dorsal turret machine gun in place (nor anyplace
on the aircraft). Subject states that the air gunner sergeants who should
occupy this fourth position are on duty with the regiment, but are engaged
in fatigue details, and XXXX rarely carried on training flights.

     Subject believes the TU-2 to be manufactured in a factory in Moscow,
and it is noted that a plaque in the aircraft stated that it had been produced
in Factory No. 19.

     A fuller report will shortly be underway, based on interrogation
conducted so far, and many more details are expected to be obtained in the
next week or two, with both pilot and navigator being interrogated.

translationJa.summaryJa: 1948年11月のAFO/USAFEの抜粋報告（TT #1524）を収めた文書。主要項目は次の通り。1) USAFE 2（機密）: 欧州軍特殊諜報組織が作成した報告書一式を整備し、資金配分の参考としてジェネラル・キャベルへ回付する旨。報告書は受領時のまま転送されたものが多く、注意を促している。2) USAFE 10（機密扱い）: 1948年9月5日1402Z、307th爆撃群の3機乗員がオランダ西岸付近（51°55'N/03°55'E、3万フィート）で未確認機を目撃。通常のジェット巡航速度から煙・凝結跡を伴い急加速・上昇し、ロケット補助を用いたように見えた。評価はB-2。3) USAFE 14（極秘）: 飛行円盤報告の再発。ノイビーベルク基地上空でのホバリング事例や、スウェーデンの技術者による湖での着水／墜落観測と、潜水隊が発見した未記載の湖底陥没を記述。スウェーデン当局は既知の地上文化によらない高い技術の可能性を示唆しており、USAFEは結論を保留して意見を求めている。4) ソ連関連（極秘）: コロミア（Kholomia）空域付近の“Redut”レーダー、射程約150kmの運用報告、TU-2所属部隊の装備（尾部IFF S.CH.(C-4)、1947年の機上レーダー実験等）、格納や滑走路整備状況、3名乗員で来着したTU-2に背部旋回銃塔が欠如していた旨、製造は工場第19号の銘板あり。追加尋問に基づく詳細報告が予定されている。5) USAFE 16（機密）: CIC情報で、ソ連が在外CSR任務に対しコストを問わず大量のレーダー管と完全なレーダー装置の購入を指示したとの報告（評価C-3）。
translationJa.summaryEn: Extracts from TT #1524 (USAFE, 4 Nov 1948) containing several intelligence items. Key points: 1) USAFE 2 (Secret): A complete set of reports from the European Command special intelligence organization has been assembled and forwarded to Gen. Cabell for inspection and disposition; caution advised as many reports were forwarded as received. 2) USAFE 10 (Confidential): At 1402Z on 5 Sep 1948, three crews of the 307th Bomb Group observed an unidentified aircraft off the west coast of Holland (51°55'N/03°55'E) at 30,000 ft; the object left smoke/condensation trails, showed sudden acceleration and climb, appeared jet-propelled with probable rocket assist; assessed B-2. 3) USAFE 14 (Top Secret): Recurring flying-saucer reports, including a ~30-minute hover over Neubiberg Air Base and a Swedish technical expert’s observation of an object that crashed/landed in a lake; Swedish salvage/divers found an uncharted depression on the lake floor and consider the observation reliable, suggesting a possibly non‑earth technology; USAFE keeps an open mind and requests reactions. 4) Soviet-related technical/airfield report (Top Secret): Presence of a Soviet 'Redut' radar near Kholomia airfield (approx. 5 km W), believed PVO-operated with ~150 km range; TU-2s of the 63rd Regiment fitted with IFF type S.CH.(C-4); 1947 airborne radar tail-warning tests conducted; Kholomia airfield described as open pasture with runway construction begun; TU-2s arriving with three-man crews and missing dorsal turret; aircraft plaque indicates Factory No. 19; further interrogation reports forthcoming. 5) USAFE 16 (Secret): CIC source reports the Russians have ordered CSR missions abroad to purchase large quantities of radar tubes and a complete radar set regardless of cost (Eval C-3).

SUMMARY (Give summary which highlights the salient factors of narrative report. Begin narrative text on AF Form 112a unless report can be fully stated on AF Form 112. List inclosures, including number of copies)

        This report contains an eye witness account of the ascent and
flight of an unconventional aircraft in the Trans Caucasus region of the
USSR. This aircraft was reported by three highly reliable United States
observers who were travelling by rail at the time of the sighting. The
three observers were firmly convinced that they saw a genuine flying
saucer or flying disc. Two sightings occurred at 1910 hours on 4 Oct. 55
between AWATY and ADZHLIABOL, ten minutes by rail after departing AWATY.
One disc aircraft ascended almost vertically, at a relatively slow speed with
its outer surface revolving slowly to the right, to an altitude of about 6000
foot where its speed then increased sharply as it headed north. The second
flying disc was seen performing the same actions about one minute later. The
take-off area was about 1-2 miles south of the rail line where two searchlight
___0___ INCLS    beams were seen pointing up almost vertically. All other
observations given to USAIRA in Prague by the three visitors, 12-13 Oct 55,
are presented in Part II. USAIRA COMMENT: The significance of this report re
the USAF project "Unidentified Flying Objects" is remarkable and lends
credence to many "saucer" reports.    Thomas S. Ryan

        QUOTED below is the cable classified Top Secret which was sent
to Hqs. USAF on 13 Oct 55. USAIRA control number is C-103 and text follows:

   "NIACT. TO: DINTA, WASH. DC. NOFORN. USAF handle as OPERATIONAL
IMMEDIATE. USAF CRYPTO PASS TO CINCUSAFE AND USAIRA MOSCOW. THREE RELIABLE
US OBSERVERS, SENATOR RICHARD RUSSELL, LT. COL. E.U. HATHAWAY, ARMY, MR.
RUBEN EFRON, VISITED PRAGUE 12-13 OCT. ARRIVING DIRECT FROM KIEV, VIA BAKU,
TIFLIS, DNIEPERPETROVSK, BLACK SEA AREA, AND REPORTED FOLLOWING TO USAIRA
AND USARMA.: ON 4 OCT. 55 AT 1910 HOURS BETWEEN ATJATI AND ADZHIJABUL, TEN
MINUTES BY RAIL AFTER DEPARTING ATJATI IN TRANS CAUCASUS REGION, TWO ROUND
AND CIRCULAR UNCONVENTIONAL AIRCRAFT RESEMBLING FLYING DISCS OR FLYING
SAUCERS WERE SEEN TAKING OFF ALMOST VERTICALLY ONE MINUTE APART. DISC
AIRCRAFT ASCENDED NEAR DUSK WITH OUTER SURFACE REVOLVING SLOWLY TO RIGHT
AND WITH TWO LIGHTS STATIONARY ON TOP NEAR MIDDLE PART. SPARKS OR FLAME
SEEN COMING FROM AIRCRAFT. NO PROTRUSIONS SEEN ON AIRCRAFT WHICH PASSED
OVER OBSERVERS' TRAIN. BOTH FLYING DISC AIRCRAFT ASCENDED RELATIVELY SLOWLY
TO ABOUT 6000 FEET, THEN SPEED INCREASED SHARPLY IN HORIZONTAL FLIGHT BOTH
ON NORTHERLY HEADING. FLYING ATTITUDE OF DISC REMAINED SAME DURING ASCENT
AS IN CRUISE, LIKE A DISCUS IN FLIGHT. TWO OPERATING SEARCHLIGHTS POINTING
ALMOST VERTICAL SEEN NEAR TAKEOFF AREA LOCATED ABOUT 1-2 MILES SOUTH OF RR
LINE. AFTER SIGHTING SOVIET TRAINMEN BECAME EXCITED AND LOWERED CURTAINS
AND REFUSED PERMISSION TO LOOK OUT WINDOWS. US OBSERVERS FIRMLY BELIEVE
THESE UNCONVENTIONAL AIRCRAFT WERE GENUINE SAUCER OR DISC AIRCRAFT. USAIRA
RATES INTO B-2. ON 9 OCT.55 AT DNIEPERPETROVSK AIRFIELD, HATHAWAY REPORTED
42 STUBBY JET FIGHTERS NOT FAGOTS AND ONE MULTI JET BOMBER DESCRIBED AS:
ONE HALF AGAIN AS LONG AS US COCOA 47; ENGINES CANVAS COVERED BURIED WING
TYPE; CANOPY WELL FORWARD NEAR BLUNT NOSE; TRICYCLE GEAR; DEFINITE
SWAYBACK SHAPE ON TOP OF FUSELAGE; SEVERELY SWEPT WINGS SET IN MIDDLE OF
FUSELAGE AND LOCATED ALMOST MIDWAY FROM NOSE TO TAIL; TAILPLANE LOCATED LOW
BENEATH BOTTOM LEVEL OF VERTICAL FIN; VERTICAL FIN SWEPT WITH SQUARE TOP;
AND SILVER BULBOUS BULGE AT TAILCONE EXTENDING REARWARD OF RUDDER LINE.
DNIEPERPETROVSK AIRFIELD WAS GRASS SOD. AT BAKU LONG TRAIN LOADED WITH
MANY PLATOON SIZE LANDING CRAFT. 42 KILOMETERS FROM MOSCOW ON MOSCOW TO
MINSK HIGHWAY,250 YARDS TO RIGHT OF ROAD, PARTY SIGHTED RADAR SITE
TENTATIVELY IDENTIFIED HERE AS ONE WOODGAGE OR GAGE AND ONE SQUARE POLE
FREYA.
   RECOMMEND COMPLETE DEBRIEFING OF RUSSELL GROUP UPON RETURN AND
SUGGEST COMMENDATION FROM D/I FOR EFFORTS. RUSSELL GROUP DEPARTED PRAGUE
ABOARD SWAISSAIR FOR ROME 13 OCT. (Signed) T.S.RYAN."

        On 12 Oct. 1955 at about 2145 hours, Sen. Russell, Lt. Col.
E.U. Hathaway, U.S. Army staff officer assigned to Senate Armed Forces
Committee, and Mr. Ruben Efron, Committee Consultant, arrived at Wilson
(Hlavni) Station in Prague, having come direct from Kiev. Their rail
route from Kiev brought them to COP, at the eastern border of Czechoslovakia,
where they observed the RR gauge switching operation from the Russian broad
gauge to the Czech standard guage. Upon arrival at the RR Wilson Station,
the Russell group was met by the acting Chief of Mission, Mr. Harold Vedler,
and the USAIRA. We escorted the group to the US Residency where they were
to spend the night. It was evident that they had seen much and had been to
places in Russia and possibly in Czechoslovakia where US observers had not
been, at least for a good many years. Sen. Russell stated that he had been
in Prague once before in 1927, and was anxious to see some familiar places.
After arrival at the Residency and dinner, Lt. Col. Hathaway expressed a
desire to report something of the utmost importance to the USAIRA, "something
you may not believe, but something that we've been told by your people (USAF)
doesn't exist." I suggested that we not discuss anything at the Residency

Army Attache. Lt. Col. Hathaway said he was anxious to report his observation
and that he had witnesses, fortunately, in Sen. Russell and Mr. Efron.
        We met at 0900 on 13 Oct. in the larger office of the Army Attache
and proceeded with the debriefing amid adequate safeguards for talking.
Present were: Lt. Col. Hathaway, Mr. Efron, Col. Dooley and myself. Col.
Dooley and I took notes and provided paper for sketches. Sen. Russell was
busy with the Chief of Mission and was unable to attend. Due to the
departure time of the group, we were unable to spend more than one hour
talking, the interview ending about 1200. Col. Hathaway did most of the
explaining and answering with Mr. Efron supplementing and adding support.
        Lt Col.Hathaway proved to be an excellent observer and Mr. Efron
had kept detailed notes which he referred to for times and places.
        Hathaway led off with "I doubt if you're going to believe this
but we all saw it. Sen. Russell was the first to see this flying saucer
and he called us to the window, and we both saw the second one (pointing to
EFRON who nodded yes). We've been told for years that there isn't such a
thing but all of us saw it, including Sen Russell. " It was emphasized
that Sen. Russell saw the first flying saucer or flying disc ascend and
pass over the train on a northerly course, taking off from the left side
of the train's direction, which places the take-off area on the south side
of the RR line on which they were travelling.
        I stated that I don't disbelieve anything after having been in
Czechoslovakia for 17 months. The following raw notes are quoted with
my additional comments after:
    1. "Two flying saucer type aircraft were seen between two railway
station stops after we left BAKU."
    2. "It was after we left ADJAR, we were there at 1900 and we saw the
aircraft at 1910. The next place we saw was ADZHIJABUL."(Efrons notes.)
    3. "They took off straight up and then the speed increased greatly
as they moved straight ahead, horizontally, and disappeared to the right of
the train." (Questioning revealed that the angle of ascent was not exactly
"straight up" but rather in a slight arc just off the vertical line.)
    4. "The whole object whirred and then levelled and zoomed off at very
high speed." (Questioning revealed that the outer surface of the object
revolved slowly in a clockwise direction or to the right, with the rate of
ascent being relatively slow in comparison to the high speed which the
object took on at when it reached altitude.)
    5. " The take off was at an angle to about 2000 meters." (Both objects
were said to have ascended almost vertically to an approximate altitude
of 6000 feet before sharply increasing speed in level flight.)
    6. "They were seen out of window on left side of train."
    7. " Two searchlight were seen pointing at an angle near where the
saucer took off." (The angle was nearly vertical and evidently, I gathered,
that the angle of one searchlight beam was nearly vertical approximating
the arc which the disc ascended to 6000 feet, while the second searchlight
beam was pointing at another spot. Lack of time prevented complete
clarification of the searchlight beams. Dusk was falling at the time of
sighting.)
    8. "Some sparking or flame came out bottom as craft rose."
    9. "After we saw the two discs, the Soviet trainmen became excited,
closing curtains and telling us that we were not allowed to look out of
windows." (The behavior of the trainmen was such as to indicate that the US
passengers had seen something that they were not supposed to see.)
    10. "Approximately one minute elapsed between the first and second
takeoffs of the aircraft." (It was explained that Sen Russell had seen the

USAIRA COMMENT: I believe that further debriefing of all three

PART B. OBSERVATIONS AT BAKU

        A long NE train comprised of flat cars was seen outside of BAKU.
Each flatcar had one landing craft which was described by Col. Hathaway
as being platoon size, with a slot in the rear for an outboard engine
and the tops of the boats covered with canvas. Men were seen in the
vicinity wearing a unique uniform which he could not recognise.
        One jet aircraft was seen flying high over Baku, too high for
any type of identification. The party landed at Baku by aircraft, the
civilian airfield being located an hour from the city. A military airfield

                PART C.    OBSERVATIONS AT DNIEPERPETROVSK AIRFIELD

                The three US observers arrived at Dnieperpetrovsk airfield
        sometime on 9 Oct. 55 by DC-3 type aircraft. The airfield is grass-sod.
        The parking ramp is of octagonal brick or cement (see sketch of jet bomber
        and ramp brick design on page 8 ). One jet bomber was parked at the airfield
        ( see description in text of cable and see profile sketch on page 8).
                Col. Hathaway counted 42 very stubby jet fighters parked at the
        field. The jet fighters were described as "short, stubby, smaller and
        higher horizontal tailplane, wings more forward, canopy more forward."
        At the time of the description I was having Col. Hathaway compare the
        fighter he saw with a scale model of a FAGOT. He definitely did not think
        they were Fagots because of the fuselage being more stubby. (Sort of rules
        out Frescos of which I could use a model as I don't have any.) This is my
        reason for citing SRI TIC 6244, as the composite configuration concludes
        that the SRI fighter is one third smaller than the MIG-15. I did not have
        time to show the composite drawing to the observer but the possibility
        exists that his sighting was of the SRI composite type. Further debriefing
        should bring out more details.

               PART F.   OBSERVATIONS AT COP AND ABOUT CZECH RAILROADS


          The Russell group arrived at COP, the RR border crossing point
between USSR and Czechoslovakia, early on the morning of 12 Oct. 55.
About 1-2 hours later at 0630, they left COP and were on their way to
Prague where they arrived at 0947 (on time)p.m. (2147 hours).
          Upon arrival at COP, the train was broken up. One car was
marked MOSCOW-BUCHAREST and was disconnected. Another car was marked
MOSCOW-PRAGUE, the group's car, sleeper, and was disconnected and taken
on a spur under a red star suspended on a border arch (probably marking
border of Czechoslovakia) into a long building on the Czech side. This
building was lighted and its length was such as to accomodate the car
and two replacement trucks. The trucks for the new Czech RR guage were of
the two axel type. The switching of trucks consumed 40-45 minutes for
their sleeper car. There was an electric switch box or panel control on
one side of the building. The passengers had to debark during the changing
of the trucks. All other train cars were marked MOSCOW-COP.
          The switching building had a pit in the middle which the car
straddled. Inside the sleeper there were two large square traps in the
cars floor, one at either end. The first step was for the crew to open
these doors and turn a large bar, which evidently released the truck from
the body of the car. The second step was to apply large jacks at four
points of the car on the outside, about at the position of the trucks,
two jacks on a side. When the car was sufficiently jacked, the Czech
guage trucks, which on the tracks forward of the car [REDACTED] on
               were
the standard guage tracks of the Czech RR which were laid inside the
Russian guage tracks, were pushed forward towards the sleeper. The Czech
trucks banged the first Russian trucks out of place, continuing to the
second Russian trucks and banging them out of place. The jacked car was
then ready to have the Czech trucks fastened. The jacks were lowered,
letting the car down to the new standard guage trucks below. The crew
then turned the bars through the floor openings locking the new trucks
in place and the passengers were informed that they could board the car.
(See sketch for USAIRA-Hathaway version of this operation.)

 leaving COP, Col. Hathaway observed very large RR marshaling yards with

        The RR route which the party travelled from COP was through

   ten minutes after COP. From Cop to Kosice, Hathaway believed that there
   were two tracks and possibly three.
        From Kosice on Hathaway stated that construction was going on
   through the mountains, the construction crews using a prefabricated
   technique. Piled up alongside of the right of way were prefabricated
   track sections with "rails already hooked to sleepers." Little buildings
   were spotted along the right of way where this prefabrication was taking
   place. Cable reels and stacks of metal towers were seen, the towers
   being rusty. He believed that electrification was nearly completed all
   the way although his train was being pulled by a steam engine.
        Just at dark, location enroute unknown, Hathaway passed by an

要約（報告の主旨が分かる要点を示すこと。本文は AF Form 112a で開始するか、AF Form 112 上で完全に述べられる場合はそれを使用する。添付物および部数を列記）

        本報告は、ソ連南コーカサス地域における非在来型航空機の上昇および飛行の目撃証言を含む。 この航空機は、当時列車で移動中であった三名の極めて信頼できる米国人観測者によって報告された。 三名の観測者は、本物の「空飛ぶ円盤」または飛行円板を見たと確信していた。 1955年10月4日1910時間に AWATY と ADZHLIABOL の間、AWATY を出発して列車で十数分後に二つの目撃があった。 一機の円盤状航空機はほぼ垂直に、比較的遅い速度で上昇し、その外表面はゆっくり右に回転し、約6000フィートの高度に達したところで速度が急激に増し北方へ向かった。 二機目の飛行円盤は約1分後に同様の動作を行うのが見られた。 離陸地点は鉄道線の南約1〜2マイルの地点で、ほぼ垂直に向けられた二つのサーチライトの光線が見えた。 全ての他の観察は、10月12〜13日にプラハで三名の訪問者から USAIRA に与えられたもので、パート II に提示されている。 USAIRA コメント: 本報告が USAF プロジェクト「未確認飛行物体」に関して持つ意義は注目に値し、多くの「円盤」報告に信憑性を与える。    Thomas S. Ryan
                                    THOMAS S. RYAN, LT. COL. AIR ATTACHE

        以下に引用するのは、1955年10月13日に本省 USAF 宛てに送付された最高機密扱いの電報である。USAIRA 管理番号は C-103 であり、本文は次の通りである:

   "NIACT. TO: DINTA, WASH. DC. NOFORN. USAF handle as OPERATIONAL
IMMEDIATE. USAF CRYPTO PASS TO CINCUSAFE AND USAIRA MOSCOW. THREE RELIABLE
US OBSERVERS, SENATOR RICHARD RUSSELL, LT. COL. E.U. HATHAWAY, ARMY, MR.
RUBEN EFRON, VISITED PRAGUE 12-13 OCT. ARRIVING DIRECT FROM KIEV, VIA BAKU,
TIFLIS, DNIEPERPETROVSK, BLACK SEA AREA, AND REPORTED FOLLOWING TO USAIRA
AND USARMA.: ON 4 OCT. 55 AT 1910 HOURS BETWEEN ATJATI AND ADZHIJABUL, TEN
MINUTES BY RAIL AFTER DEPARTING ATJATI IN TRANS CAUCASUS REGION, TWO ROUND
AND CIRCULAR UNCONVENTIONAL AIRCRAFT RESEMBLING FLYING DISCS OR FLYING
SAUCERS WERE SEEN TAKING OFF ALMOST VERTICALLY ONE MINUTE APART. DISC
AIRCRAFT ASCENDED NEAR DUSK WITH OUTER SURFACE REVOLVING SLOWLY TO RIGHT
AND WITH TWO LIGHTS STATIONARY ON TOP NEAR MIDDLE PART. SPARKS OR FLAME
SEEN COMING FROM AIRCRAFT. NO PROTRUSIONS SEEN ON AIRCRAFT WHICH PASSED
OVER OBSERVERS' TRAIN. BOTH FLYING DISC AIRCRAFT ASCENDED RELATIVELY SLOWLY
TO ABOUT 6000 FEET, THEN SPEED INCREASED SHARPLY IN HORIZONTAL FLIGHT BOTH
ON NORTHERLY HEADING. FLYING ATTITUDE OF DISC REMAINED SAME DURING ASCENT
AS IN CRUISE, LIKE A DISCUS IN FLIGHT. TWO OPERATING SEARCHLIGHTS POINTING
ALMOST VERTICAL SEEN NEAR TAKEOFF AREA LOCATED ABOUT 1-2 MILES SOUTH OF RR
LINE. AFTER SIGHTING SOVIET TRAINMEN BECAME EXCITED AND LOWERED CURTAINS
AND REFUSED PERMISSION TO LOOK OUT WINDOWS. US OBSERVERS FIRMLY BELIEVE
THESE UNCONVENTIONAL AIRCRAFT WERE GENUINE SAUCER OR DISC AIRCRAFT. USAIRA
RATES INTO B-2. ON 9 OCT.55 AT DNIEPERPETROVSK AIRFIELD, HATHAWAY REPORTED
42 STUBBY JET FIGHTERS NOT FAGOTS AND ONE MULTI JET BOMBER DESCRIBED AS:
ONE HALF AGAIN AS LONG AS US COCOA 47; ENGINES CANVAS COVERED BURIED WING
TYPE; CANOPY WELL FORWARD NEAR BLUNT NOSE; TRICYCLE GEAR; DEFINITE
SWAYBACK SHAPE ON TOP OF FUSELAGE; SEVERELY SWEPT WINGS SET IN MIDDLE OF
FUSELAGE AND LOCATED ALMOST MIDWAY FROM NOSE TO TAIL; TAILPLANE LOCATED LOW
BENEATH BOTTOM LEVEL OF VERTICAL FIN; VERTICAL FIN SWEPT WITH SQUARE TOP;
AND SILVER BULBOUS BULGE AT TAILCONE EXTENDING REARWARD OF RUDDER LINE.
DNIEPERPETROVSK AIRFIELD WAS GRASS SOD. AT BAKU LONG TRAIN LOADED WITH
MANY PLATOON SIZE LANDING CRAFT. 42 KILOMETERS FROM MOSCOW ON MOSCOW TO
MINSK HIGHWAY,250 YARDS TO RIGHT OF ROAD, PARTY SIGHTED RADAR SITE
TENTATIVELY IDENTIFIED HERE AS ONE WOODGAGE OR GAGE AND ONE SQUARE POLE
FREYA.
   RECOMMEND COMPLETE DEBRIEFING OF RUSSELL GROUP UPON RETURN AND
SUGGEST COMMENDATION FROM D/I FOR EFFORTS. RUSSELL GROUP DEPARTED PRAGUE
ABOARD SWAISSAIR FOR ROME 13 OCT. (Signed) T.S.RYAN."

        1955年10月12日約2145時間、Russell 上院議員、Lt. Col. E.U. Hathaway（陸軍、上院軍事委員会に配属された幕僚）、および Mr. Ruben Efron（委員会顧問）は、キエフから直行してプラハの Wilson（Hlavni）駅に到着した。キエフからの鉄路は、チェコスロバキア東端の国境にある COP に至り、そこで彼らはロシアの広軌からチェコの標準軌への軌間切替作業を観察した。 Wilson 駅到着時、Russell 一行は臨時団長 Mr. Harold Vedler と USAIRA に迎えられた。我々は一行を宿泊することになっている米国公館に案内した。彼らは多くの場所を見て回っており、米国の観測者が少なくとも近年行っていない場所にも行っているのが明らかだった。Russell 上院議員は以前1927年にプラハを訪れたことがあり、懐かしい場所を見たいと言っていた。公館到着後の夕食の後、Lt. Col. Hathaway は USAIRA に極めて重要なことを報告したいと述べ、「あなた方は信じないかもしれないが、米空軍が存在しないと言っているものだ」と言った。私は公館でこれを議論しないよう提案した。

because of the absence of security precautions but suggested that we meet
early the next morning in my office together with Col. Thomas Dooley , the US
Army Attache. Lt. Col. Hathaway said he was anxious to report his observation
and that he had witnesses, fortunately, in Sen. Russell and Mr. Efron.
        We met at 0900 on 13 Oct. in the larger office of the Army Attache
and proceeded with the debriefing amid adequate safeguards for talking.
Present were: Lt. Col. Hathaway, Mr. Efron, Col. Dooley and myself. Col.
Dooley and I took notes and provided paper for sketches. Sen. Russell was
busy with the Chief of Mission and was unable to attend. Due to the
departure time of the group, we were unable to spend more than one hour
talking, the interview ending about 1200. Col. Hathaway did most of the
explaining and answering with Mr. Efron supplementing and adding support.
        Lt Col.Hathaway proved to be an excellent observer and Mr. Efron
had kept detailed notes which he referred to for times and places.
        Hathaway led off with "I doubt if you're going to believe this
but we all saw it. Sen. Russell was the first to see this flying saucer
and he called us to the window, and we both saw the second one (pointing to
EFRON who nodded yes). We've been told for years that there isn't such a
thing but all of us saw it, including Sen Russell. " It was emphasized
that Sen. Russell saw the first flying saucer or flying disc ascend and
pass over the train on a northerly course, taking off from the left side
of the train's direction, which places the take-off area on the south side
of the RR line on which they were travelling.
        I stated that I don't disbelieve anything after having been in
Czechoslovakia for 17 months. The following raw notes are quoted with
my additional comments after:
    1. "Two flying saucer type aircraft were seen between two railway
station stops after we left BAKU."
    2. "It was after we left ADJAR, we were there at 1900 and we saw the
aircraft at 1910. The next place we saw was ADZHIJABUL."(Efrons notes.)
    3. "They took off straight up and then the speed increased greatly
as they moved straight ahead, horizontally, and disappeared to the right of
the train." (Questioning revealed that the angle of ascent was not exactly
"straight up" but rather in a slight arc just off the vertical line.)
    4. "The whole object whirred and then levelled and zoomed off at very
high speed." (Questioning revealed that the outer surface of the object
revolved slowly in a clockwise direction or to the right, with the rate of
ascent being relatively slow in comparison to the high speed which the
object took on at when it reached altitude.)
    5. " The take off was at an angle to about 2000 meters." (Both objects
were said to have ascended almost vertically to an approximate altitude
of 6000 feet before sharply increasing speed in level flight.)
    6. "They were seen out of window on left side of train."
    7. " Two searchlight were seen pointing at an angle near where the
saucer took off." (The angle was nearly vertical and evidently, I gathered,
that the angle of one searchlight beam was nearly vertical approximating
the arc which the disc ascended to 6000 feet, while the second searchlight
beam was pointing at another spot. Lack of time prevented complete
clarification of the searchlight beams. Dusk was falling at the time of
sighting.)
    8. "Some sparking or flame came out bottom as craft rose."
    9. "After we saw the two discs, the Soviet trainmen became excited,
closing curtains and telling us that we were not allowed to look out of
windows." (The behavior of the trainmen was such as to indicate that the US
passengers had seen something that they were not supposed to see.)

（翻訳）
安全対策が欠如しているためにそうできなかったが、翌朝早く、米陸軍武官の Col. Thomas Dooley と一緒に私の事務所で会うことを提案した。Lt. Col. Hathaway は自分の観察を報告したがっており、幸い証人として Sen. Russell と Mr. Efron がいると述べた。
        我々は10月13日0900に陸軍武官の広い事務所で会い、会話のための十分な保護のもとで聴取を行った。出席者は：Lt. Col. Hathaway、Mr. Efron、Col. Dooley、および私であった。Col. Dooley と私はメモを取り、スケッチ用の用紙を用意した。Sen. Russell は在任官（Chief of Mission）と面会中で出席できなかった。グループの出発時間のため、我々は1時間以上話すことができず、インタビューは約1200に終了した。説明と回答の大部分は Col. Hathaway が行い、Mr. Efron が補足して支持を加えた。
        Lt. Col. Hathaway は優れた観察者であることが判明し、Mr. Efron は時刻と場所を参照する詳細な記録を保持していた。
        Hathaway は「信じないだろうと思うが、我々は皆それを見た。Sen. Russell がこれを最初に見て窓に呼び、我々は二つ目のものも見た（EFRON を指して頷かせる）。何年もそんなものはないと言われてきたが、Sen. Russell を含む我々全員がそれを見た」と切り出した。重要なのは、Sen. Russell が最初の飛行円盤（flying saucer または flying disc）が上昇して列車の上を北寄りの進路で通過するのを見ており、それは列車の進行方向の左側から発進したため、発進地点は彼らが移動していた鉄道路線の南側に位置する、という点であった。
        私は、チェコスロバキアに17か月間いた後では何も信用しないわけではないと述べた。以下の一次メモはそのまま引用し、私の追加コメントを後に付す：
    1. 「BAKU を出発した後、二つの鉄道駅の間で二つの飛行円盤型航空機が見られた。」
    2. 「ADJAR を出発した後で、我々はそこに1900にいて、1910に航空機を見た。次に見た場所は ADZHIJABUL だった。」（Efron のメモ）
    3. 「それらは真っ直ぐ上に離陸し、その後速度が大幅に増して水平にまっすぐ進み、列車の右側へ消えた。」（質問により、上昇角は正確に「真っ直ぐ上」ではなく、垂直線からわずかに外れた弧を描いていたことが明らかになった。）
    4. 「物体全体がビュンと鳴ってから水平になり、非常に高速度で飛び去った。」（質問により、物体の外面はゆっくり時計回り、すなわち右方向に回転しており、上昇の速度は比較的遅かったが、一旦高度に達すると極めて高い速度をとったことが明らかになった。）
    5. 「離陸は約2000メートルまでの角度で行われた。」（両方の物体はほぼ垂直に上昇しておよそ6000フィートの高度に達し、その後水平飛行で急速に速度を増したとされる。）
    6. 「それらは列車の左側の窓から見えた。」
    7. 「円盤が離陸した場所の近くで角度をつけて照射している二つの探照灯が見られた。」（角度はほぼ垂直であり、私が理解したところでは、一方の探照灯のビームの角度はほぼ垂直で、円盤が6000フィートに上昇した弧に近似しており、二つ目の探照灯ビームは別の地点を照らしていた。探照灯ビームの完全な解明は時間不足でできなかった。目撃時は薄暮になりつつあった。）
    8. 「上昇する際に底部から火花または炎が出た。」
    9. 「二つの円盤を見た後、ソビエトの列車員は興奮し、カーテンを閉め、窓の外を見ることは許されないと言った。」（列車員の行動は、米国の乗客が見てはいけない何かを見たことを示すものであった。）
    10. 「航空機の最初と二番目の離陸の間には約1分経過した。」（Sen Russell は最初の飛行物体を見て、それが全く違ったものだと認識し、Mr. Efron と Col. Hathaway に見せようと急いだと説明された。Col. Hathaway は上院議員と一緒に窓に到達して最初のものを見たと言い、Mr. Efron は混雑のため最初のものは短くしか見られなかったと言った。しかし三人とも二番目の円盤を見ており、皆が最初と同じ丸い円盤状航空機、すなわち最初のものと同じものを見たと一致している。）
11. 「離陸地点は約1マイル離れていた、少し遠いかもしれない。」（探照灯は同じ地域にあった。）
12. 「円盤の中心寄りに二つの灯があり、外面が回転している間もそれらは静止していた。」（両者はこの点で断固として同意した。#）「灯は円盤の上部近くにあった。」（もし円盤の直径を表す線を三分割すると、灯は中央部分と外側二部分の境目、すなわち分割点の二か所に位置したであろう。すなわち、Mr Efron の助けを借りて描かれたスケッチ参照：

                    RELATIVE POSITION
                        OF 2 LIGHTS

13. 「航空機は円形だった。」 「航空機は丸かった。」 「飛行円盤に似ていた。」 「円盤の形、円形で、右回りもしくは時計回りに回転しているように見えた。」（これら二人の観察者の目には明確に円形、あるいは少なくとも円状であり、突出部や「棒」や膨らみはなかったとされる。厚さや直径の見積もりはどちらの観察者からも得られなかった。）
14. 「目立った色はなかった」（薄暮のため色の印象は得られなかったと述べられた。）
15. 「2000メートルに達した後、左から右、すなわち南から北へ向かって大きな速度で飛び去った。」（上昇時と巡航時の速度差は非常に顕著であった。）
16. 「我々の左、すなわち列車の南側の地平線で離陸を見ていた。」
17. 「外周部はゆっくり右に回転していた。」（登攀中と水平飛行に移った後では円盤の動きに対する印象が異なり、上昇時には「ゆっくり回転」という語が使われ、巡航飛行時には「ビュン」という表現が使われた。）
18. #"「円盤は速度を上げて飛び去ったときと同じ姿勢で上昇した。」飛行円盤の飛行姿勢は投擲円盤（discus）の飛行に似ているとされた。）

USAIRA COMMENT: I believe that further debriefing of all three
US observers in a more relaxed atmosphere and with more time would
produce much more valuable technical details than the hurried interview
above.

PART B. OBSERVATIONS AT BAKU

        A long NE train comprised of flat cars was seen outside of BAKU.
Each flatcar had one landing craft which was described by Col. Hathaway
as being platoon size, with a slot in the rear for an outboard engine
and the tops of the boats covered with canvas. Men were seen in the
vicinity wearing a unique uniform which he could not recognise.
        One jet aircraft was seen flying high over Baku, too high for
any type of identification. The party landed at Baku by aircraft, the
civilian airfield being located an hour from the city. A military airfield

Baku の外で、平底貨車（フラットカー）からなる長い北東行きの列車が見られた。各フラットカーには一艇の上陸艇が載っており、Col. Hathaway の説明では小隊規模で、船尾に舷外機用のスロットがあり、艇の上部はキャンバスで覆われていた。周辺で見られた人々は独特の制服を着ており、彼は識別できなかった。
        Baku 上空には一機のジェット機が高高度で飛行しているのが見られ、識別には高すぎた。一行は飛行機で Baku に着陸した。民間飛行場は市から1時間の距離に位置していた。軍用飛行場は

（原文続く）
        市の郊外で民間飛行場へ向かう途中に通過した。
        Intourist のガイドはこれが軍用訓練飛行場であると述べ、Col. Hathaway はそこに駐機していた濃緑色の輸送機のいくつかを認識した。

                PART C.    OBSERVATIONS AT DNIEPERPETROVSK AIRFIELD

                The three US observers arrived at Dnieperpetrovsk airfield
        sometime on 9 Oct. 55 by DC-3 type aircraft. The airfield is grass-sod.
        The parking ramp is of octagonal brick or cement (see sketch of jet bomber
        and ramp brick design on page 8 ). One jet bomber was parked at the airfield
        ( see description in text of cable and see profile sketch on page 8).
                Col. Hathaway counted 42 very stubby jet fighters parked at the
        field. The jet fighters were described as "short, stubby, smaller and
        higher horizontal tailplane, wings more forward, canopy more forward."
        At the time of the description I was having Col. Hathaway compare the
        fighter he saw with a scale model of a FAGOT. He definitely did not think
        they were Fagots because of the fuselage being more stubby. (Sort of rules
        out Frescos of which I could use a model as I don't have any.) This is my
        reason for citing SRI TIC 6244, as the composite configuration concludes
        that the SRI fighter is one third smaller than the MIG-15. I did not have
        time to show the composite drawing to the observer but the possibility
        exists that his sighting was of the SRI composite type. Further debriefing
        should bring out more details.


（翻訳）
                PART C.    DNIEPERPETROVSK 飛行場での観察

                3名の米国人観察者は 1955年10月9日頃に DC-3 型機で Dnieperpetrovsk 飛行場に到着した。飛行場は芝土である。駐機ランプは八角形のレンガまたはセメントでできている（ジェット爆撃機とランプのレンガ設計のスケッチは8ページ参照）。飛行場には1機のジェット爆撃機が駐機していた（ケーブル本文の説明および8ページのプロファイルスケッチ参照）。
                Col. Hathaway は駐機している非常にずんぐりしたジェット戦闘機を42機数えた。ジェット戦闘機は「短く、ずんぐりしており、小型で、水平尾翼が高く、主翼が前寄り、キャノピーが前寄り」と説明された。説明の際、私は Col. Hathaway に彼が見た戦闘機を FAGOT の縮尺模型と比較してもらっていた。彼は胴体がよりずんぐりしているため、それらが Fagot だとは断定的に思わなかった。（私が持っていない Fresco 型を除外するようなものだ。）これが私が SRI TIC 6244 を引用する理由であり、複合構成図は SRI 戦闘機が MIG-15 より三分の一小さいと結論づけている。観察者に複合図を見せる時間はなかったが、彼の目撃が SRI 複合型であった可能性は存在する。さらなる事情聴取でより詳細が明らかになるはずである。

        PART D.    OBSERVATIONS NEAR MOSCOW

                The three observers were escorted to a place which Senator Russell
        had requested to see outside Moscow. On the way, exactly at the 42 kilometer
        signpost from Moscow on the Moscow to Minsk highway, on the right side
        of the road, there was a radar site (size unknown) with two radars. From
        the sketches of Col. Hathaway, they have been tentatively identified as
        one Woodgage or Gage and one square type [ILLEGIBLE] Freya. (See sketch below):
        (Approx. 200-250 yards off side of road.) POLE


        [SKETCHES OF TWO RADAR INSTALLATIONS]


（翻訳）
        PART D.    モスクワ近郊での観察

                3名の観察者は、Senator Russell がモスクワ郊外で見たいと要請した場所に案内された。途中、モスクワからミンスクへ向かう幹線道路のモスクワから42キロの標識のちょうど地点で、道路の右側にレーダーサイト（規模不明）と二つのレーダーがあった。Col. Hathaway のスケッチから、それらは仮に一基が Woodgage または Gage、もう一基が方形タイプの [ILLEGIBLE] Freya と同定された。（道路脇から約200–250ヤードの位置。）POLE

        [二つのレーダー施設のスケッチ]


        PART E.    OBSERVATIONS FROM TIFLIS TO SOCI.

AT TIFLIS about the 5th of Oct. 55, Col. Hathaway sighted a
        large helicopter resembling a banana with two large, main rotors at each
        end and having many more windows than a banana type which he had seen in
        the USA.
                Between TIFLIS AND SOCI, on the Black Sea, while travelling by
        train, one of the most significant coincidences occurred, taking into
        account the observations which were reported in the ATJATY region. Sen.
        Russell's party made contact with a Russian who was about 55 years, named
        EGOROV. He was accompanied by a younger engineer who job was to keep
        EGOROV supplied with spirits. EGOROV was feeling pretty good when he met

               PART F.   OBSERVATIONS AT COP AND ABOUT CZECH RAILROADS


          The Russell group arrived at COP, the RR border crossing point
between USSR and Czechoslovakia, early on the morning of 12 Oct. 55.
About 1-2 hours later at 0630, they left COP and were on their way to
Prague where they arrived at 0947 (on time)p.m. (2147 hours).
          Upon arrival at COP, the train was broken up. One car was
marked MOSCOW-BUCHAREST and was disconnected. Another car was marked
MOSCOW-PRAGUE, the group's car, sleeper, and was disconnected and taken
on a spur under a red star suspended on a border arch (probably marking
border of Czechoslovakia) into a long building on the Czech side. This
building was lighted and its length was such as to accomodate the car
and two replacement trucks. The trucks for the new Czech RR guage were of
the two axel type. The switching of trucks consumed 40-45 minutes for
their sleeper car. There was an electric switch box or panel control on
one side of the building. The passengers had to debark during the changing
of the trucks. All other train cars were marked MOSCOW-COP.
          The switching building had a pit in the middle which the car
straddled. Inside the sleeper there were two large square traps in the
cars floor, one at either end. The first step was for the crew to open
these doors and turn a large bar, which evidently released the truck from
the body of the car. The second step was to apply large jacks at four
points of the car on the outside, about at the position of the trucks,
two jacks on a side. When the car was sufficiently jacked, the Czech
guage trucks, which on the tracks forward of the car [REDACTED] on

Russian guage tracks, were pushed forward towards the sleeper. The Czech
trucks banged the first Russian trucks out of place, continuing to the
second Russian trucks and banging them out of place. The jacked car was
then ready to have the Czech trucks fastened. The jacks were lowered,
letting the car down to the new standard guage trucks below. The crew
then turned the bars through the floor openings locking the new trucks
in place and the passengers were informed that they could board the car.

translationJa.summaryJa: 米空軍駐在武官作成の航空情報報告書 IR 193-55（情報日付 1955年10月4日、作成日 1955年10月14日）。上院議員リチャード・ラッセル、陸軍大佐 E.U. ハサウェイ、顧問ルーベン・エフロンの三名が列車移動中にソ連南コーカサス（アトヤティ／アジジヤブル間）で非在来型の円盤状航空機を目撃したとの目撃証言を記載。1955年10月4日 19:10 頃、列車左側の南方約1–2マイルの地点から1分間隔で二機がほぼ垂直に上昇し、外面が右回りにゆっくり回転、上昇して約6000フィート付近で速度を急増して北方へ水平飛行で飛び去った。機体上部に二個の静止した灯、上昇時に機体下部から火花または炎が見えた。離陸付近でほぼ垂直を向けた二つのサーチライトが観測され、現地の列車員は興奮してカーテンを閉め外を見せなかった。報告は USAIRA 電報 C-103（1955年10月13日送信）として HQ USAF に伝えられ、作成者 Lt. Col. Thomas S. Ryan は本件を B-2 と評価。付随して、ハサウェイはドニエプロペトロフスク空港で「スタビー」型のジェット戦闘機42機および多発ジェット爆撃機1機の目撃を報告している。デブリーフはプラハで1955年10月12–13日に実施。
translationJa.summaryEn: Air Intelligence Information Report IR 193-55 (date of information 4 Oct 1955; prepared 14 Oct 1955) from the US Air Attache. Three reliable US observers—Senator Richard Russell, Lt. Col. E.U. Hathaway (Army), and Mr. Ruben Efron—reported witnessing two unconventional round/circular (disc or saucer) aircraft while traveling by train in the Trans-Caucasus between Atjati and Adzhijabul at about 1910 hours on 4 Oct 1955. The two discs took off about one minute apart from a takeoff area roughly 1–2 miles south of the railroad, ascended almost vertically (to approximately 6,000 feet) with the outer surface rotating slowly to the right, showed two stationary lights near the top/midsection, and emitted sparks or flame from the bottom during ascent. Upon reaching altitude each sharply increased speed and flew north in level flight. Two searchlights pointing nearly vertically were observed near the takeoff area. Soviet trainmen reacted by closing curtains and preventing further observation. USAIRA transmitted these facts in cable C-103 (13 Oct 1955) and Lt. Col. Thomas S. Ryan rated the report B-2. The report also records Hathaway's separate observation at Dnieperpetrovsk airfield of 42 stubby jet fighters and one multi-jet bomber. The debriefing occurred in Prague on 12–13 Oct 1955.

     1.  In compliance with Flight Service Regulation 200-4, dated
2 November 1948, Subject:  "Unidentified Flying Objects," the follow-
ing report is submitted.

     2.  On the night of 6 January 1950, two objects were sighted over
Kansas City, Kansas, and Olathe, Kansas.  They appeared to be motionless
over Olathe for ten to fifteen minutes, then moved off very fast.

     3.  The weather at Kansas City was clear with twelve miles visi-
bility.

     4.  The incident was witnessed by James F. Grey, 6200 Hadley St.,
Raytown, Missouri, phone FL 2744; and Robert Van De Vyvere, 5532, Raytown
Road, Missouri.  Both are employed at Bendix Aviation, Kansas City, Kansas,
and the former is a pilot.

     5.  Photos are not available.  Sketches are enroute to Lowry Flight
Service and will be forwarded immediately upon receipt.

     6.  Two objects were sighted, both spherical in shape.  They ap-
peared to be the size of old fashioned street lights about two blocks
distant.  They were a brilliant white, emanating orange and red flashes.

     7.  They moved from over Kansas City toward Olathe, Kansas, remained
motionless from ten to fifteen minutes, then moved off very fast in a
southwesterly direction.  The estimated altitude was between seven and
eight thousand feet.  No sound was emitted, nor exhaust trail apparent.

     8.  This report was given to Fairfax AFB Operations, Kansas City,
Kansas, and transmitted to Lowry Flight Service.

     1. Deputy U.S. Marshal Paul HERRING, Kodiak, Alaska, reported to the Intelli-
gence Officer on 11 April 1949 that he observed a celestial manifestation cross-
ing the sky above the U.S. Naval Operating Base, Kodiak, Alaska, 8 April 1949 at
approximately 2030 hours. According to Mr. HERRING, he saw a flaming greenish-
blue object plummet across the sky at an altitude of 2,500 feet at an estimated
speed of 1,500 miles per hour. This disturbance, stated Mr. HERRING, was first
observed above Anton Larson Bay, (See Enclosure (A)), moving from West to East on
a course that approximately paralleled the East-West runways of the U.S. Naval
Air Station, Kodiak, Alaska, and was visible for approximately 15 seconds when the
flame disappeared in the vicinity of Puffin Island, Chiniak Bay. In the opinion
of Mr. HERRING, the object was not a meteor as it was too large and there were no
sparks which are generally observed associated with such phenomena. He stated
that his first impression was that it was either a jet fighter or that an air-
craft was on fire. This opinion was dissipated when he

     1.  In compliance with FS Regulation 200-4, subject "Unidentified
Flying Objects" dated 2 November 1948, in reference to letter, Headquarters,
USAF, subject: "Reporting of Information on 'Flying Discs,'" dated
6 February 1948, the following report is submitted.

     2.  An unidentified flying object was seen over Fort Worth, Texas,
on 13 April 1949, at approximately 2105C, by 1st Lt Robert A. Francis,
who called it to the attention of Captain Stanley Borowski.  Both
officers are assigned to the Carswell Flight Service Center, Carswell
Air Force Base, Fort Worth, Texas.

     3.  Subject officers had just returned from a local flight and
were standing by their aircraft on the flight line.  The weather at
time object was sighted reported by Carswell Air Force Base was clear
and visibility of eight miles.  No photographs are available.  Object
was round and in the shape of a ball, very silver in color.  It was
traveling at a tremendous rate of speed, estimated to be over 1000
miles per hour, altitude was very hard to judge and cannot be estimated
correctly; however, object seemed to be clearly visible.  Lieutenant
Francis saw the object appear on the horizon in the north northwest
direction, it seemed to fly horizontally in the direction of south
southeast.  It did not appear to burn out, but suddenly disappeared.
No sound was heard.  The exhaust trail seemed to be approximately three
times the size of the object and also was silver in color.  The exhaust
consisted of silver streaks and star shaped figures.  The object definitely
did not appear to be a jet or meteor.  Its speed was far in excess of
any jet speed witnessed by officers.  The entire sighting took place
in a matter of a few seconds.  A check of the Carswell Flight Service
flight following racks showed no jet aircraft flying in this area at
time object was sighted.

     1.  In accordance with Restricted letter, Headquarters, 2108th Air
Weather Group, subject:  Report on Information on "Flying Discs", dated
24 March 1948, the following report is submitted.

     2.  At 2030 hours on 8 February 1949, Captain McBride of the S. S.
Antigua, A United Fruit vessel, berthed at Cristobal pier area, Canal
Zone, was interviewed by Intelligence personnel, Caribbean Air Command,
concerning three aerial objects sighted by officers of his ship on voy-
age to Canal Zone from New Orleans, Louisiana.

     3.  Captain McBride stated that the first object, which appeared to
be a disc, was sighted at 1630 on 6 February 1949 at 12 degrees 30 minutes
north latitude, 81 degrees 10 minutes west latitude, in the close vicinity
of the San Andres Islands.  The S. S. Antigua's course was 152 degrees at
16 knots.  When sighted, the object was at an altitude of 60 degrees from
the horizon as determined by the ship's sextant in the direction of 120
degrees.  As it passes directly over the ship, several officers described
it as a round, silver-colored sphere.  Although McBride had difficulty in
determining its height, he estimated the diameter as 12 to 14 inches.  As
it passed overhead, bearing 310 degrees, it changed color from silver to
yellow to red and went out of sight in the dusk at an altitude of 22 de-
grees.  The wind at the time was estimated at force four, approximately
29.

     4.  At 1700 on the same date two more objects were sighted, one off
the port bow at an altitude between 50 and 60 degrees, and the other off
the starboard bow bearing 201 degrees at an altitude of 47 degrees.  Both
disappeared abeam in the dusk.  None showed any luminousity or motivating
power.

     5.  The circumstances described suggest a possibility that these
objects are some type of weather balloons.  A study made by this head-
quarters of the prevailing winds at all altitudes during the period 4-6
February 1949 virtually eliminate any possibility of a radiosonde instru-
ment being the object sighted.  The only release point which might have

                                        Jan. 27th, 1949.
                                        GMO., Tokyo

     In addition to the previous report on the glow from the

     1.  Iida Weather Station.
     Last night, we have observed in this district a phenomenon,

it.
     At Iida, at 19h 46m 30s, a pale glow was observed in the
direction of Northeast at an altitude of 35° above the horizon,
which moved almost horizontally through north toward west and
then disappeared.  This glow was as great as one and a half of
the moon in diameter with considerable brightness.  At about
19h 50m, a heavy sound was heard and doors trembled.  This pheno-
menon have been observed in many places in the district of this
station, of which report will be made after investigation.

     2.  Suwa Weather Station.
     At 19h 50m on 25th, a pale glow like meteor with a sound was
observed at Suwa.  This glow appeared in a distance of a few
degree to the north-north-east of Betelguese in the Orion Constel-
lation and moved almost to southeast, attaining its maximum
brightness at an altitude of about 60° above horizon.  It shined
with palish white colour, the intensity of which was such that
objects on the ground near the observer were clearly discernible
for a moment illuminated by it.  Thereafter, it became yellowish
in colour, then yellowish red passing a point in the southwest
and at an altitude of about 40°, and finally disappeared.  The
time elapsed for the above was 3 or 4 seconds.  About 1 minute
thereafter, a sound resembling to a distant thunder was heard,
which continued for about 15 seconds.

     3.  Nagano Weather Station.
     At about 19h 50m on January 25th, a phenomenon, probably be
a meteor, with a sound like that of explosion was observed in
many places near this station.  According to the observation taken
by Yasuo Miyamoto, a member of this station, a glow appeared
in the direction of east-south-east and at a point of medium
altitude above horizon, which moved sending out palish white
light toward a point in the direction of west-south-west, where
it disappeared below the horizon.  This glow continued about
5 minutes.  About 3 minutes thereafter, a sound like that of
explosion was heard in the direction of west-south-west.

SUBJECT:  Sighting of "Flying Discs"

     A strong possibility exists that the "flying disc" might have been a piece of
cardboard, or light metallic substance carried aloft by the funneled air currents
over Hickam.

     The nearby cane fields give off a considerable amount of moisture, thereby
creating a "dead space."  The prevailing winds striking this area are directed up-
ward over the field, and hence could carry inanimate objects up with them.

     Then, too, the altitude given could be considerably off, inasmuch as the ob-
ject sighted was thin.  Judging heights of such objects is difficult enough, even
if the object were 3 - 4 feet in thickness.

     Suggest you check records of Air Weather Service for confirmation of wind
peculiarities over Hickam.

1949 at 1407 local time and went out of sight at approximately 1435 local
time.  The object was first sighted by Capt. Stoney when it was approxi-
mately 25 miles due east of Hickam.  There were scattered clouds at 3500
feet (base) and the visibility at the time was approximately 20 miles plus.
Capt. Stoney is the Assistant S-2 Officer of the 1810th AACS Group located
at Hickam Field, T. H., and is also a twin-engine pilot.  No photographs
are available due to the fact that Capt. Stoney was not in possession of a
camera at the time and had no idea that he would have sufficient time to
procure one.  In the words of Capt. Stoney, the object appeared to be a
large round piece of flat white cardboard, oscillating continually.  The
object sighted was the only one seen and appeared to approximate the size
of an AT-6.  Capt. Stoney stated that the object seemed to be extremely
white on the underside, while the topside portion of the object seemed to
have a dark, non-reflecting surface.  The speed of the object was approxi-
mated at 85 miles per hour.  Capt. Stoney further stated that the object
circled the area, making right circles and left circles at approximately

     3.  Capt. Stoney reported the presence of a C-54 type aircraft in the

     4.  Capt. Stoney reported that, at all times and during the departure

     5.  When object ultimately departed on a straight course, it appeared

of climb approximated 25 degrees.  Witness stated that it was extremely
difficult to approximate the rate of speed during departure due to the dis-

that it was his opinion that this object was under absolute control at all
times and that definite gyrations were being executed.  The turns were ex-

* STATEMENT *

12 January 1949

     At the request of Chief of Intelligence, the undersigned wishes
to describe as accurately as possible his impressions of the brief ap-
pearance of an unknown illuminated object which appeared over Fairfield-
Suisun AFB at 2015 PST on 3 December 1948.  The object first shot into
view about 2 miles north of the control tower, flying at a low altitude
between 500 and 1000 feet, climbing on a low trajectory, with a speed
estimated at something in excess of 400 miles per hour.  Immediately
after sighting, this observer rushed to the east side of the tower.  By
this time the object was estimated to have not more than 1500 feet of
altitude and its speed had slowed for several seconds to perhaps two-
hundred (200) miles per hour.  The observer can recall that at this
stage the object had a very slight undulating or bouncing motion.
When its position oriented with a line between the tower and the air
freight terminal, but a slight distance east of the terminal, the ob-
ject took an almost vertical rise or climb and levelled off again at
an estimated three thousand feet.  At that time the other control
tower operator on duty continued watching the object while this ob-
server telephoned the AACS operations officer residing on the base in
hopes he might be able to get a look at it.  The other tower operator
reported the object almost immediatly afterwards started a fast climb
toward the south-southeast and reached about twenty thousand feet, at
which point he lost sight of it.  The undersigned never saw the object
again after going for the telephone.
     Pertinent information is that the light was clearly seen with the
naked eye, brilliant but by no means blinding.  In size it was comp-
arable to one of Fairfield-Suisun AFB's high-intensity runway lights.
The observer is convinced it was not an aircraft navigation light.  The
night was clear, and the wind was indicating southwest at 10 miles per
hour on tower instruments.
     I certify and affirm that the information herein is true and ac-
curate to the best of my knowledge and ability.

     I, James E. Doty, Sergeant, USAF, AF 17171864, Weather Observer,
16th Weather Squadron, Chanute Air Force Base, Chanute Field, Illinois,
do hereby make the following statement to Captain Rush T. Kelley,
Assistant Base Weather Officer.

     On 8 December 1948 at approximately 1546 hours, I was walking
with Sgt. Eugene B. Montag towards the Base Weather Station when I
happened to look up at the sky and notice what appeared to be either
a sky rocket or meteor. I tapped Sgt. Montag on the arm and called
his attention to it.

     The object did not appear to be a star because it was three or
four times as large as a star and it seemed to be closer to us than
a star would be. It was heading from the north east toward the
south south west and was moving upwards at about 15 or 20 degree angle.
As it moved it seemed to get larger, and it was leaving a trail. In
about two or three seconds it disappeared. The object was round, white
and moved very fast.

     We went into the Weather Station and reported this to the Duty
Forecaster whose name is M Sgt. Robert N. Fillman.

     I, Eugene E. Montag, AF 16208708, Sergeant, USAF, am a Weather
Observer assigned to the 16th Weather Squadron, Chanute Air Force
Base, Chanute Field, Illinois, and do hereby make the following

     On 8 December 1948 at approximately 1846 hours, I was walking
with Sgt. James H. Doty, also of the 16th Weather Squadron, towards
the Base Weather Station when I noticed what appeared to be a sky
rocket or meteor. This object was heading upwards about a 15 degree
angle, moving from the north east to the south south west. The
object was white in color, very bright and moved about two to three
tenths of the sky and then disappeared.

     This object did not appear to me to be a falling star.

8.  本報告はFairfax AFB Operations, Kansas City, Kansasに伝えられ、Lowry Flight Serviceへ送信された。

1. 副米国保安官 Paul HERRING（コディアック、アラスカ）は、1949年4月11日に情報将校へ報告し、1949年4月8日約2030時、米海軍作戦基地コディアック（アラスカ）上空を横切る天体の現象を観測したと述べた。HERRING氏によれば、緑がかった青色に燃える物体が高度約2,500フィートで空を急降下し、推定速度1,500マイル／時で通過するのを見たという。HERRING氏は、この現象は最初にAnton Larson Bay上空（別紙（A）参照）で観測され、西から東へ、コディアック海軍航空基地の東西滑走路とほぼ平行する進路で移動し、約15秒間見えたのち、Chiniak BayのPuffin Island付近で炎が消えたと述べた。HERRING氏の見解では、その物体は流星ではなく、あまりにも大きく、通常そうした現象に伴って見られる火花がなかったためだという。彼は当初、その物体はジェット戦闘機か、航空機が炎上しているのではないかと考えたが、この意見は次のような事情により薄れた。

BRIEF:    1949年4月8日夜、米海軍作戦基地（Kodiak, Alaska）上空を通過する発光現象が観測された。

NOTE:     本情報は1949年4月8日時点のものである。

SPECIAL NOTE:  Intelligence File Index, 1948 Editionには本報告に関連する天文現象や気象現象に関する索引が含まれていないため、本報告に関連するIndex Guide Numberは組み込まれていない。

ENCLOSURE:  (A)Paul Herringが作製した図のフォトスタティックコピー（1949年4月8日の大気撹乱の進路を示す）。

1. 2.  Lieutenant Commander D. SHEPARD, USN（Operations Officer, U.S. Naval Operating Base, Kodiak, Alaska）は、NOB郵便局付近に立っていた際に、1949年4月8日約2040 hoursに「Old Woman Mountain付近の空を横切る奇妙な物体」を観察したと報告した。SHEPARDはその物体を、直径約二（2）フィートの赤みを帯びた火の玉で、高度推定2,500 feetで西から東へ移動していると表現した。「その物体は尾を伴わない鮮烈な色で、21度から20度の間の平坦な下降軌道で移動していた。Chiniak Bay上空で分解したように見えた」とSHEPARDは述べた。SHEPARDはその物体の性質についての意見は示さなかった。

3.  Lawrence B. SHAW（タクシー運転手、Arrow Cab, Kodiak, Alaska）は、1949年4月8日、Enlisted Mens ClubからAdministration Buildingへ向かう途中、約2035 hoursに空を横切る奇妙な明るい青色の物体を見たと述べた。SHAWにとってその物体は直径約1-1/2フィートに見え、三（3）フィートの尾を引いており、その尾は「ピンクがかった色合い」だった。SHAWの報告によれば、この物体はOld Woman Mountain上空に現れ、西から東へのコースを移動し、高度は約2,500 feetと推定された。約25度で高度を下げており、そのコースのまま進めばNyman Peninsula沖のChiniak Bayに衝突したであろう。SHAWには、物体がNyman Peninsulaを越えていくにつれて明るい粒子が物体から飛び散り分解したように見えたという。SHAWは、自分が見た物体はこれまで何度も見た流星や流れ星ではないと強く確信している。

4.  Paul KREUGER（バス運転手、U.S. Naval Operating Base, Kodiak, Alaska）は、1949年4月8日、2045 hoursにバスを運転中、Old Woman Mountain付近からNyman Peninsula（西から東方向）へ向かって空を横切る奇妙な緑がかった青色の閃光を観察したと報告した。KREUGERはその物体を直径1-1/2フィート、長さ約10フィートと表現した。彼は、物体がAir Stationのハンガー#8の上空を通過したときの高度は約500 feetであり、Nyman Peninsula沖のChiniak Bayに着水したであろうが、半島を越えたところで視界から消えたと述べた。「大きな緑がかったトレーサー弾のような外観だった」とKREUGERは述べた。

5.  U.S. Navy Weather Central（U.S. Naval Operating Base, Kodiak, Alaska）は、1949年4月8日2000 hoursの天候を次のように報告した。

    Ceiling:          3,000 feet, scattered clouds, 3/10 coverage.
    Visibility:       15 miles.
    Wind:             North-Northwest, 15 knots.
    Temperature:      27 degrees.

6.  観察者から物体の発する音に関する報告はなかった。

1.  FS Regulation 200-4（"Unidentified Flying Objects"）1948年11月2日付、並びに米空軍本部の書簡（"Reporting of Information on 'Flying Discs,'" dated 6 February 1948）に基づき、以下の報告を提出する。

2.  1949年4月13日約2105C、Carswell Flight Service Center（Carswell Air Force Base, Fort Worth, Texas）に所属する1st Lt Robert A. FrancisがFort Worth, Texas上空で未確認飛行物体を目撃し、Captain Stanley Borowskiに注意を喚起した。両将校はCarswell Flight Service Centerに配属されている。

3.  対象将校はちょうど地元飛行から戻り、滑走路の自分たちの航空機の近くに立っていた。物体が目撃された時点での天候はCarswell Air Force Baseの報告によれば快晴、視程8マイルであった。写真はない。物体は球形で非常に銀色に見えた。物体は非常に速い速度で飛行しており、時速1,000マイルを超えると推定される。高度は判断が困難で正確に推定できないが、物体は明瞭に見えていたようである。Francis中尉は物体が北北西方向の地平線上に現れ、南南東方向へ水平に飛行していったように見えたと述べた。物体は燃え尽きたようには見えず、突然消失した。音は聞かれなかった。排気の跡は物体の約3倍の大きさで、これも銀色に見えた。排気は銀色の筋と星形の図形から成っているようであった。物体は明らかにジェットや流星ではなかった。将校が目撃したどのジェットの速度よりもはるかに速かった。目撃全体は数秒で終了した。Carswell Flight Serviceの飛行監視記録を調査したところ、物体が目撃された時間にこの地域を飛行しているジェット機はなかった。

SUBJECT:  Unidentified Aerial Objects Vicinity of San Andres Islands,

TO:       Commanding General
          Military Air Transport Service
          Washington 25, D. C.
          ATTENTION: AC/S, A-2


     1.  In accordance with Restricted letter, Headquarters, 2108th Air
Weather Group, subject:  Report on Information on "Flying Discs", dated
24 March 1948, the following report is submitted.

     2.  At 2030 hours on 8 February 1949, Captain McBride of the S. S.
Antigua, A United Fruit vessel, berthed at Cristobal pier area, Canal
Zone, was interviewed by Intelligence personnel, Caribbean Air Command,
concerning three aerial objects sighted by officers of his ship on voy-
age to Canal Zone from New Orleans, Louisiana.

     3.  Captain McBride stated that the first object, which appeared to
be a disc, was sighted at 1630 on 6 February 1949 at 12 degrees 30 minutes
north latitude, 81 degrees 10 minutes west latitude, in the close vicinity
of the San Andres Islands.  The S. S. Antigua's course was 152 degrees at
16 knots.  When sighted, the object was at an altitude of 60 degrees from
the horizon as determined by the ship's sextant in the direction of 120
degrees.  As it passes directly over the ship, several officers described
it as a round, silver-colored sphere.  Although McBride had difficulty in
determining its height, he estimated the diameter as 12 to 14 inches.  As
it passed overhead, bearing 310 degrees, it changed color from silver to
yellow to red and went out of sight in the dusk at an altitude of 22 de-
grees.  The wind at the time was estimated at force four, approximately
29.

     4.  At 1700 on the same date two more objects were sighted, one off
the port bow at an altitude between 50 and 60 degrees, and the other off
the starboard bow bearing 201 degrees at an altitude of 47 degrees.  Both
disappeared abeam in the dusk.  None showed any luminousity or motivating
power.

     5.  The circumstances described suggest a possibility that these
objects are some type of weather balloons.  A study made by this head-
quarters of the prevailing winds at all altitudes during the period 4-6
February 1949 virtually eliminate any possibility of a radiosonde instru-
ment being the object sighted.  The only release point which might have

     In addition to the previous report on the glow from the

     1.  Iida Weather Station.
     Last night, we have observed in this district a phenomenon,

it.
     At Iida, at 19h 46m 30s, a pale glow was observed in the
direction of Northeast at an altitude of 35° above the horizon,
which moved almost horizontally through north toward west and
then disappeared.  This glow was as great as one and a half of
the moon in diameter with considerable brightness.  At about
19h 50m, a heavy sound was heard and doors trembled.  This pheno-
menon have been observed in many places in the district of this
station, of which report will be made after investigation.

     2.  Suwa Weather Station.
     At 19h 50m on 25th, a pale glow like meteor with a sound was
observed at Suwa.  This glow appeared in a distance of a few
degree to the north-north-east of Betelguese in the Orion Constel-
lation and moved almost to southeast, attaining its maximum
brightness at an altitude of about 60° above horizon.  It shined
with palish white colour, the intensity of which was such that
objects on the ground near the observer were clearly discernible
for a moment illuminated by it.  Thereafter, it became yellowish
in colour, then yellowish red passing a point in the southwest
and at an altitude of about 40°, and finally disappeared.  The
time elapsed for the above was 3 or 4 seconds.  About 1 minute
thereafter, a sound resembling to a distant thunder was heard,
which continued for about 15 seconds.

     3.  Nagano Weather Station.
     At about 19h 50m on January 25th, a phenomenon, probably be

many places near this station.  According to the observation taken
by Yasuo Miyamoto, a member of this station, a glow appeared
in the direction of east-south-east and at a point of medium
altitude above horizon, which moved sending out palish white
light toward a point in the direction of west-south-west, where

* STATEMENT *

12 January 1949

     情報部長の依頼により、下記署名者は1948年12月3日2015 PSTにFairfield-Suisun AFB上空に現れた未確認発光物体の短時間の出現について、自身の印象を可能な限り正確に記述したい。物体は最初に管制塔の北約2マイルの地点で出現し、地上高度500～1000フィートの低い高度を飛行し、低軌道で上昇し、その速度は秒速でなく時速で推定400マイル超であった。発見直後、当観測者は塔の東側へ急いだ。時点としては物体は推定で高度1500フィート程度しかなく、その速度は数秒間おそらく時速200マイル程度まで遅くなっていたことを記憶している。観測者はこの段階で物体がわずかにうねるような、あるいはバウンドするような動きをしていたことを覚えている。
     物体が塔と航空貨物ターミナルを結ぶ線上の位置に来たとき、しかしターミナルよりわずかに東の地点で、物体はほぼ垂直に上昇し、推定3000フィートで再び水平飛行になった。その時点で当直の他の管制塔オペレーターは物体の観察を続け、当観測者は基地内に住んでいるAACS運用士官に電話をかけ、彼がそれを見ることができるかもしれないと望んだ。もう一方の塔オペレーターはほぼ直後に物体が南南東へ向けて速い上昇を開始し約20,000フィートに達し、その地点で視界から外れたと報告した。下記署名者は電話に行った後、物体を二度と見なかった。
     関連事項として、光は裸眼で明確に見え、きらびやかであったが決して目をくらますほどではなかった。大きさはFairfield-Suisun AFBの高輝度滑走路灯の一つに相当すると見積もられる。観測者はそれが航空機の航法灯ではなかったと確信している。夜は晴朗で、塔の計器では風は南西10マイル/時を示していた。
     ここに記載した情報は、私の知識と能力の範囲で真実かつ正確であることを証明し、断言する。

translationJa.summaryJa: 文書は複数の未確認飛行物体（UFO）目撃報告を含む。主な事案は次の通り。1) 1950年1月6日（Lowry, 9 Jan 1950宛）— Kansas CityおよびOlathe上空で夜間に2個の球形物体が目撃された。Olathe上空で約10–15分静止していたように見え、その後南西へ非常に速く移動。明るい白色で橙・赤の閃光を発し、推定高度7,000–8,000フィート。音や排気尾は確認されず。写真なし、スケッチ送付中。目撃者はBendix Aviation勤務のJames F. Grey（パイロット）ら。2) 1949年9月20日（Olmsted, 22 Sep 1949）— C-45機の乗員（Lt Col Phillip J. Kuhlほか）が43°40'N 74°55'W付近で銀色の円筒形物体を観測。当初20,000フィートにありゆっくり降下して7,000フィートの雲に消失。橙色・白色の炎状の尾が物体長の2倍以上に見え、推進はロケットまたはジェット様と記載。音は聞かれず。写真なし。3) 1949年8月22日（McChord, 23 Aug 1949）— シアトル周辺で複数の管制官・AR T C職員による目撃報告。報告の一つは直径75–100フィート、深さ10–15フィートの光沢あるアルミ色の円形物体で高度約10,000フィート、速度推定500–600mph、北から南へ移動、音はジェット機に類似とされるが排気痕は確認されなかった。別の報告ではF-84に類似する物体が4–5千フィートで南から北へ移動（音なし）。写真・スケッチは得られていない。目撃者にはSgt Jack Faulkner、T/Sgt T. D. Mullen、Sgt Roger H. Studeman、Ben Frieman、Howard Watsonら。4) 1949年8月15日（Maxwell, 16 Aug 1949）— Greenville, S.C.上空で丸く灰色の物体が目撃され、推定高度5,000フィート以下、音や排気痕はなし。316th Troop Carrier Wingの調査で、テネシー州で放出された地球気象担当の気球と結論付けられた。各報告とも写真はほとんど得られておらず、物理的証拠は提示されていない。
translationJa.summaryEn: The documents contain multiple UFO sighting reports. Key incidents: 1) 6 Jan 1950 (Lowry): Two spherical objects sighted over Kansas City and Olathe at night. They appeared motionless over Olathe for about 10–15 minutes, then departed very rapidly to the southwest. Described as brilliant white with orange/red flashes, estimated altitude 7,000–8,000 ft. No sound or exhaust trail noted. No photographs; sketches en route. Witnesses included James F. Grey (pilot) and Robert Van De Vyvere. 2) 20 Sep 1949 (Olmsted): Lt Col Phillip J. Kuhl and crew aboard a C-45 observed a silvery cylindrical object at approx. 43°40'N 74°55'W. It descended slowly from ~20,000 ft and disappeared into overcast at ~7,000 ft. An orange/white flame trail more than twice the object's length was reported; propulsion described as rocket- or jet-like. No sound reported. No photographs. 3) 22 Aug 1949 (McChord / Seattle area): Multiple controllers and ARTC personnel reported sightings. One report described a circular, shiny aluminum object ~75–100 ft diameter and 10–15 ft deep at ~10,000 ft, estimated speed 500–600 mph, moving north-to-south; sound likened to a jet by some observers but no exhaust trail was confirmed. Another report described an object resembling an F-84 at 4–5,000 ft moving south-to-north with no sound. No photos/sketches obtained. Witnesses named include Sgt Jack Faulkner, T/Sgt T. D. Mullen, Sgt Roger H. Studeman, Ben Frieman, and Howard Watson. 4) 15 Aug 1949 (Maxwell / Greenville, S.C.): A round gray object was seen moving northeast below ~5,000 ft with no sound or exhaust trail. The 316th Troop Carrier Wing concluded it was a weather balloon released in Tennessee. Photographs and physical evidence were generally not available in these reports.
